prompt:
Use case: identity-preserve
Asset type: one production character turnaround reference sheet for future 3D modeling, NOT a new character design and NOT a 3D render.
Input image 1: authoritative original Pierrot female character illustration from the game; preserve the character's identity, proportions, costume construction, palette, and illustration technique.

Primary request: depict THIS EXACT ADULT WOMAN in three aligned full-body views on one wide landscape sheet: front view on the left, strict rear view in the center, strict right-facing side profile on the right. The sheet is for checking the previously unseen back before building a model. In all three views use the same upright neutral relaxed A-pose, feet separated slightly, knees straight, hands slightly clear of hips, arms only about 20 degrees out from the torso. Consistent head-to-body ratio and identical scale; tops of heads and heels aligned. In the profile keep the arm slightly clear so the torso contour can be understood. No perspective distortion. Full hair, hands, coat tails, and shoes inside frame with margins.

Identity locks: same adult anime woman, elegant face, narrow crimson eyes, fair skin, short voluminous wavy crimson bob with swept asymmetric part and layered neck-length curls; NOT long hair, NOT a new haircut, NOT a doll or realistic human. Preserve her original adult proportions without exaggerating or flattening anatomy.

Costume locks: original off-shoulder white ruffled neckline; black ruffled choker and crimson star/bow at front; detached voluminous red/white/black harlequin-diamond sleeves ending in black ruffled cuffs and small gold star fasteners; original fitted black-and-white bodice with red trim and connected gold star fastenings over the front openings; original black pointed hip/bodysuit sections; pale/white thigh-high legwear with LARGE crimson diamond pattern, decorated black/crimson high-heeled shoes with gold stars and straps. Preserve the elaborate flowing split black/crimson/white long fabric tails attached around the hips and their small gold star finials. Fabric must have readable separate layers and actual continuous attachment to the garment; settle the tails naturally with mild separation rather than dramatic wind. Do not replace them with a single generic cape, skirt, rear bow or armor. Infer only the unseen rear construction conservatively: fitted black rear bodice following the existing seams and thin red/gold trim; split tails hang from the back/side waist, consistent with the front. Preserve patterned sleeves and legwear as they wrap around the body. No newly invented large insignia, jewelry, straps, shoulder armor, new colors or extra equipment. Keep original coverage; do not make costume more revealing.

Weapon: omit the lance from all three views so it does not occlude anatomy or become fused to the hand in later modeling. The original lance will be modeled separately; do NOT redesign or replace it.

Style: match original polished 2D anime-fantasy game illustration, crisp delicate contours, rich but controlled black/crimson/white and gold accents, broad painted/cel shading, clear elegant fabric folds, same fine face and hair rendering. Retain costume complexity without random microtexture, glitter, grain or photorealistic skin. NOT a plastic 3D figurine, NOT a simplified mannequin, NOT chibi.

Backdrop and light: plain uniform very light warm-gray background, no scene, no checkerboard, no floor pedestal, no red atmospheric halo, no graphic frame. Soft neutral even lighting with readable material colors; no strong rim light or dramatic cast shadows. This is visual design reference, not a finished relightable texture map.
Text: only small restrained labels below the three views: "PRZÓD", "TYŁ", "PROFIL". No heading, watermark, notes or extra inset portraits.
Priority: fidelity to original character and consistency between the three views over inventing new design details.
